neighbours.label: narration of time passing or growing late (hours had gone by, it was already evening, it was getting dark)
fire: By the time the ferry docked it was already nearly midnight.
Three long days had gone by and still no letter came.
We kept digging until it started getting dark over the ridge.
Hours slipped past while the old men played cards on the porch.
It was already evening when the doctor finally rode in.
A whole week had passed since anyone had seen the captain.
The afternoon wore on and the shadows grew longer across the yard.
Before she knew it, the morning was gone and nothing was packed.
quiet: When the ferry docked a porter carried our bags up the hill.
Three long tables stood in the hall and every chair was full.
We kept digging until we struck a flat rock under the ridge.
Stories were told while the old men played cards on the porch.
The doctor finally rode in with a bag of clean bandages.
A whole crew was needed to lift the anchor for the captain.
The yard was wide and a fence ran along its eastern side.
She looked around the room, and nothing was packed in the trunk.
